classification.difficultyReason: Identify the changing upper boundary, split the shaded region at the intersection and add two definite integrals.

content.prompt: Find the areas of the shaded regions. You will need to find two areas and add.

spec.description: Two upward-opening parabolas with equation labels and arrowheads; the region above the x-axis and below their inner branches is shaded.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (-2,0) and (2,0); intersection (0,4). The upper boundary of the shaded region is (x+2)^2 on [-2,0] and (x-2)^2 on [0,2]. No grid or numerical y-axis ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: All curves, equation labels, axis labels, vertex labels and shading are permanent question givens.

answer.worked:
The curves intersect where
$$\begin{aligned}(x+2)^2&=(x-2)^2\\x^2+4x+4&=x^2-4x+4\\8x&=0\\x&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The shaded region has upper boundary $y=(x+2)^2$ on $[-2,0]$ and $y=(x-2)^2$ on $[0,2]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-2}^{0}(x+2)^2\,dx+\int_{0}^{2}(x-2)^2\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{(x+2)^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{0}+\left[\frac{(x-2)^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{2}\\&=\left(\frac83-0\right)+\left(0-\frac{-8}{3}\right)\\&=\frac{16}{3}\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Two upward-opening parabolas, shaded inner region above the x-axis, equation labels with curved leaders and an intersection-coordinate label with a leader arrow.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (0,0) and (3,0); intersection (3/2,9/4). The shaded upper boundary is x^2 on [0,3/2] and (x-3)^2 on [3/2,3]. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: The coordinate label, equation labels, leaders, shading and axis labels are permanent question givens.

answer.worked:
Split the region at the given intersection, $x=\frac32$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^{3/2}x^2\,dx+\int_{3/2}^{3}(x-3)^2\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{3/2}+\left[\frac{(x-3)^3}{3}\right]_{3/2}^{3}\\&=\left(\frac98-0\right)+\left(0-\frac{-9}{8}\right)\\&=\frac94\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$
